title: Schneider Electric to buy US software firm PTC in $22.6 billion deal
source_used: TradingView (Stocktwits) and New York Post (Reuters text); Reuters page blocked
key_facts: Schneider Electric will acquire PTC for $22.6 billion in cash, $205 per share, a 42.3% premium to PTC's Friday close.
PTC shares rose over 34% premarket on Monday; Schneider shares fell 8.3% in Paris (Investing.com's headline says 7%).
It is Schneider's largest acquisition; closing is expected by the third quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals; PTC's board approved and plans to recommend it.
Schneider CEO Olivier Blum called it 'the industry's most complete software and AI powerhouse'.
Funding: up to 6 billion euros of new shares and up to 17 billion euros of debt, backed by a bridge facility from Morgan Stanley and Société Générale.
Schneider expects about 250 million euros in annual cost savings by year three and about 800 million euros in revenue gains.

The Financial Times reported talks on Sunday 4 Oct 2026 (about $20 billion); PTC's market value was $15.63 billion per LSEG data. PTC makes software used to design, manufacture and service industrial products.
quote_evidence: Schneider will pay $205 per PTC share, a 42.3% premium to the stock’s Friday closing price.

Schneider CEO Olivier Blum said the deal will create “the industry’s most complete software and AI powerhouse,” while PTC CEO Neil Barua said the company will gain scale and resources to accelerate innovation and expand its geographic footprint.
why_it_matters_hint: The deal puts factory-design software and industrial AI under one big owner; markets reacted sharply.
event_date: Announced Mon 5 Oct 2026; FT reported talks Sun 4 Oct 2026
notes: Reuters and Investing.com pages gave no readable text. Facts from Stocktwits via TradingView and New York Post (carrying Reuters text on the FT report). Synergy and premium figures are Schneider claims.
